title: UI Kit compatibility backlog: Safari touch momentum, table virtual-scroll and chart axis clipping
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Collect and triage a focused backlog of UI Kit compatibility issues observed across Safari (iOS/macOS), Firefox, and mobile WebViews. This ticket aggregates several linked mini-issues discovered during the February responsive test pass and defines next steps for design fixes, token adjustments, and eng tickets. Goal: reduce visible regressions for components used in high-traffic pages (tables, charts, primary buttons) and unblock a Dedicated customer pilot that surfaced some of the worst cases.
problem_summary: Multiple visual and interaction bugs surfaced in cross-browser QA: (1) button hit areas and micro-truncation on Safari mobile after density token scale + border-radius token interplay; (2) sticky table header jitter and row clipping in Firefox when virtual-scroll is enabled; (3) chart axis labels clipping on high-DPI Safari and overflow differences across browsers; (4) inconsistent focus ring and accessible hit targets after token compression.
impact: Medium to High: affects user workflows on admin dashboards and analytics pages. Also blocks a Dedicated pilot on iOS WebView where charts don't render full Y-axis at certain sizes. Customer impact: medium. UX confidence is low for production rollout of the responsive token scale change until these are mitigated.
reproduction_steps: Buttons: On iPhone 13 / iOS 16.4 Safari, navigate to /settings -> click a compact primary button with density token set to -1. Observe truncated left touch target when border token is 1px and button uses icon-left spacing.

Tables: In Firefox 119 on macOS, open the large dataset table with virtual-scroll enabled (page size > 500 rows) and scroll quickly. Observe sticky header jitter (1-4px) during momentum and occasional row clipping near container bottom.

Charts: On macOS Safari 16.5 with display scaling set to 125% or Retina, load the line chart on /dashboard. Axis tick labels on the left are clipped; resizing the window temporarily fixes layout until a redraw occurs.

Focus rings: In both Safari and Firefox, keyboard-tabbing to compact buttons sometimes shows the ring offset by token-based outline-offset value, causing apparent mismatch with visual button boundary.
Notes: Problems reproduce intermittently in WebView containers (Android/iOS) with different compositor behaviors; consider test matrix including Android WebView 118 and iOS WKWebView 16.4+.
acceptance_criteria: Design has produced updated token suggestions (spacing, outline-offset, border) documented with visual diffs and token fallbacks for mobile Safari
Engineering tickets created for the three highest-impact bugs with clear reproduction steps and linked PRs
Regression tests added to visual QA harness (Percy story + local replay steps) covering: compact button hit area, table virtual-scroll jitter, and chart axis clipping
Verification checklist executed on target devices (iOS 15/16, macOS Safari latest, Firefox latest, Android WebView) with screenshots attached and pass/fail recorded
Changes approved by PM (Sofia Alvarez) and Design lead (Liam O'Neill) before merge
proposed_designer_actions: Produce a small token experiment: reduce compact horizontal padding by 1px but increase hit-area via ::before expansion for Safari only as a stop-gap
Create fallback CSS for outline-offset: use a token-based clamp() with max 4px to avoid offset mismatch on high-DPI browsers
Generate visual spec pages (Confluence) showing before/after for each affected component and include retina screenshots
Mark components that need engineering feature flags for rollout (buttons.compact.safari-fix, tables.virtual-scroll-snapfix, charts.axis-redraw)
Provide copy for QA steps and attach expected screenshots for automation assertions
engineering_followups: ENG-23109: table virtual-scroll header jitter investigation and patch (create a stable scroll anchor / avoid subpixel repaint thrash)
ENG-23110: chart redraw on resize/scale to force device-pixel-ratio aware layout and remeasure axis bounds
ENG-23111: compact button hit-area polyfill for Safari iOS using pointer-events and pseudo element approach
ENG-23112: add visual regression scenarios to CI (Percy) for affected components and include device emulation settings
